arguments.content:
Advancements and Survival Trends in U.S. Cancer Care

Over the last few decades, the United States has seen significant improvements in cancer survival due to enhanced screening protocols and the development of targeted therapies. According to recent data from the American Cancer Society, the overall five-year survival rate for all cancers combined has reached approximately 70%, a milestone reflecting a 33% drop in the cancer death rate since 1991. Despite these gains, survival outcomes vary drastically based on the specific type of malignancy, with common high-mortality cancers and rare, less-studied diseases continuing to present unique clinical challenges.

* Pseudomyxoma peritonei (~100 cases per year)
* Esthesioneuroblastoma (~160 cases per year)
* Adrenocortical carcinoma (~600 cases per year)
* Chordoma (~1,000 cases per year)
* Alveolar soft part sarcoma (~1,200 cases per year)

* Glioblastoma [7%]
* Mesothelioma [12%]
* Esophagus [22%]
* Liver and Intrahepatic Bile Duct [23%]
* Lung and Bronchus [27%]
